featureFocus: Frontend Display and Navigation for Courses, Sections, and Items
documentationReport:
## Frontend Display and Navigation for Courses, Sections, and Items

This feature cluster manages the display and navigation of courses, sections, and individual learning items within the Xikolo web application. It heavily relies on data fetched from the `Xikolo::CourseService` microservice via ACFS (Asynchronous Client-side Fetching System) and uses a presenter-based architecture for rendering complex views.

### Course Display (`Course::CoursesController`)

The `Course::CoursesController` handles the primary course overview page. The `show` action is responsible for orchestrating the data fetching and presentation for a given course [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb]. It includes several `before_action` filters to ensure canonical URLs, redirect from public course pages if disabled, and set no-cache headers [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].

Key data fetched and presented on the course page includes:
*   **Teacher Information:** Retrieved using `Course::TeacherListPresenter.for_course` [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].
*   **Sections:** All sections belonging to `the_course` are fetched. A flag `@show_section_info` is set if any section has a description, influencing the view's rendering [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].
*   **Featured Items:** A list of featured video items (`content_type: 'video'`, `featured: true`) is fetched and presented using `FeaturedItemPresenter` [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].
*   **Course Previews and Details:** `CourseLargePreviewPresenter` and `Course::CourseDetailsPresenter` are used to build comprehensive views of the course, including enrollment status and meta tags for SEO [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].

The `resume` action allows users to quickly navigate to their last visited or the first available item in a course. It queries the `Xikolo::Course::Item` service for the 'current' item based on the user and course context [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb]. If no redirectable item is found, it redirects back to the course path with a notice [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb].

Course eligibility checks (`check_course_eligibility`) ensure that only published courses are accessible, or if not published, only by users with `course.content.access` permission [Source: app/controllers/course/courses_controller.rb]. Anonymous users attempting to access restricted content are redirected to the course URL and prompted to log in [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb].

### Section Display and Navigation (`SectionsController`)

`SectionsController` manages the listing and display of course sections. The `index` action is primarily for content editors, displaying all sections for a course, distinguishing between legacy and new course structures [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb]. It uses `CoursePresenter` and `Xikolo::Course::Section.new` for creating new sections [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb].

The `show` action redirects the user to the first available item within a section. If no item is available but the user has `course.content.access` permission, it redirects to the item with the minimum position [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb]. For sections with `alternative_state: 'parent'`, it renders a dedicated view using `SectionPresenter` [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb].

Administrative actions like `create`, `update`, `destroy`, and `move` for sections are also handled here, requiring `ensure_content_editor` authorization [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb]. Section creation can also involve creating implicit tags in the `Xikolo::PinboardService` [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb].

### Item Display and Management (`ItemsController`)

`ItemsController` is responsible for displaying individual course items and handling their creation, editing, updating, moving, and deletion. The `show` action is the core for displaying item content. It uses `ItemPresenter.lookup` to determine the appropriate presenter for the item's `content_type` (e.g., `video`, `rich_text`, `quiz`, `lti_exercise`) [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb, app/presenters/item_presenter.rb].

Before rendering, it performs several checks:
*   **Item Prerequisites:** If `required_items` are present and not fulfilled, a 'requirements' view is rendered [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb]. Item prerequisites mean that other items must be visited or completed with a certain score (default 50% for assessments) before access is granted [Source: services/course/app/models/item.rb]. Surveys cannot be required items as they lack scores [Source: services/course/app/models/item.rb].
*   **Visits:** A `Xikolo::Course::Visit` record is created for the user and item, unless it's a quiz or the user is masquerading/unauthenticated [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].
*   **Meta Tags:** Page title and meta tags are set based on the item presenter [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].

The `new`, `edit`, `create`, `update`, `move`, and `destroy` actions provide a comprehensive interface for content editors to manage items. This includes handling different content types, their specific parameters, and interactions with other microservices like `Xikolo::QuizService` for quizzes [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb]. Item movement supports both legacy and tree-based course structures [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb]. Deletion of items also involves deleting their associated content from respective services [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].

### Course Syllabus (`Course::SyllabusController`)

The `Course::SyllabusController` presents an overview of the course content. Its `show` action builds `Course::ProgressPresenter` for the current user and course [Source: app/controllers/course/syllabus_controller.rb]. It renders with a `course_area_two_cols` layout [Source: app/controllers/course/syllabus_controller.rb]. The `check_course_eligibility` method is overridden to allow access in `open_mode` even if the user is not enrolled, provided `Xikolo.config.open_mode['enabled']` is true, the course is not invite-only or hidden, and there are previewable items [Source: app/controllers/course/syllabus_controller.rb].

### Course Progress (`Course::ProgressController`)

`Course::ProgressController` displays the progress of a user within a course. The `show` action fetches user details (either `current_user` or a specified `user_id` if the `current_user` has `course.course.teaching` permission) and then uses `Course::DocumentsPresenter` and directly queries the `course_api` for progress data [Source: app/controllers/course/progress_controller.rb]. Item styling on the learner dashboard is distinct for surveys, non-graded items, and quizzes/exercises, indicating completion, warning, or critical states based on submission and score percentages [Source: app/presenters/course/progress_presenter.rb].

### Context and Navigation Helpers

`CourseContextHelper` and `ItemContextHelper` are crucial for establishing the context of the current course, section, and item. They define `inside_course` and `inside_item` macros that set layout, perform eligibility checks, and load navigation components [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb, app/helpers/item_context_helper.rb].

*   `CourseContextHelper` provides `the_course`, `the_section`, and `the_item` methods, which lazily load resources from the `Xikolo::CourseService` [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb]. It also includes logic for checking item and section availability based on `effective_start_date`, `effective_end_date`, and `published` status [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb].
*   `load_section_nav` in `CourseContextHelper` builds the `Navigation::TableOfContents` for the course, including current section and item, which is then used in the frontend for navigation [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb].
*   `ItemContextHelper` ensures the requested item belongs to the given course and creates `Course::PositionPresenter` and `ItemPresenter` instances for the current item [Source: app/helpers/item_context_helper.rb].

### Presenters

Presenters are heavily used to encapsulate view logic and format data for display:
*   **`ItemPresenter`:** A base class for all item types, providing common attributes and methods like `partial_name`, `redirect?`, `unlocked?`, `path`, `type_label`, `icon_class`, `css_classes`, `status_type`, `locked?`, `visited?`, `active?`, `meta_tags`, and `with_time_effort?` [Source: app/presenters/item_presenter.rb]. It also handles `required_items` using `Course::RequiredItemPresenter` [Source: app/presenters/item_presenter.rb]. Deadlines for course content elements are managed automatically in background jobs and represented by `NextDate` resources, which have a `type`, `date`, and `title`, and can be general or user-specific [Source: services/course/app/models/next_date.rb].
*   **`SectionPresenter`:** Provides attributes and methods for sections, including `items` (fetching items for the section), `available?`, `unlocked?`, `alternatives?`, and `required_sections` [Source: app/presenters/section_presenter.rb]. It also handles fetching `section_choices` for alternative sections [Source: app/presenters/section_presenter.rb].
*   Other presenters like `Course::TeacherListPresenter`, `FeaturedItemPresenter`, `CourseLargePreviewPresenter`, `Course::CourseDetailsPresenter`, `Course::DocumentsPresenter`, `Course::ProgressPresenter`, `CoursePresenter`, `Course::LayoutPresenter`, `Course::PositionPresenter`, `Course::RequiredItemPresenter`, and `Course::RequiredSectionPresenter` are used to structure and format specific parts of the UI.

### Technical Debt and Limitations
*   The `current_user` passed to `Course::DocumentsPresenter` for feature checks might be an admin/teacher monitoring progress, not the actual user, which is noted as needing refactoring [Source: app/controllers/course/progress_controller.rb].
*   The `ItemsController#create` and `update` actions have inconsistencies in error handling between content types, with some errors displayed as flash messages and others inline [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].
*   The `ItemsController#create_video_uploads!` method has a TODO to reuse passed-in upload IDs [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].
*   Item prerequisites have known limitations: Survey quizzes cannot be required items, deletion of required items is not handled gracefully, and locked/unpublished items should not be required [Source: services/course/app/models/item.rb].
*   The `SectionsController#create` action has a TODO regarding null values for dates [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb].
*   The `SectionsController#show` action's redirect logic for alternative sections needs improvement for logged-in vs. anonymous users [Source: app/controllers/sections_controller.rb].
*   The `CourseContextHelper#check_course_eligibility` has a TODO to improve checks [Source: app/helpers/course_context_helper.rb].
*   The `open_mode` restriction to video items is temporary and will be removed later [Source: app/controllers/items_controller.rb].

Overall, the frontend display and navigation system is complex, leveraging a microservice architecture with extensive use of presenters and helpers to manage data flow and UI logic. It provides robust functionality for both learners and content editors, with identified areas for future improvement and refactoring.

class SectionsController < ApplicationController
  responders Responders::ApiResponder,
    Responders::DecorateResponder,
    Responders::HttpCacheResponder,
    Responders::PaginateResponder

def index
    sections = Section.all
    sections.where! course_id: params[:course_id] unless params[:course_id].nil?
    sections.where! published: params[:published] unless params[:published].nil?
    sections = sections.available unless params[:available].nil?
    sections.where! id: params[:id] if params[:id]
    sections.where! position: params[:position] if params[:position]
    if params[:parent_id]
      sections.where! parent_id: params[:parent_id]
    elsif !params[:include_alternatives]
      sections = sections.not_alternative
    end
    sections.includes! :course

    respond_with sections
  end

def show
    respond_with Section.find params[:id]
  end

def create
    section = Section.create section_params

class SectionChoicesController < ApplicationController
  responders Responders::ApiResponder,
    Responders::DecorateResponder,
    Responders::HttpCacheResponder,
    Responders::PaginateResponder

  respond_to :json

  def index
    choices = SectionChoice.all
    choices.where! user_id: params[:user_id] if params[:user_id]
    choices.where! section_id: params[:section_id] if params[:section_id]
    respond_with choices
  end

  def create
    sc = SectionChoice.find_or_initialize_by(user_id: params[:user_id],
      section_id: params[:section_id])
    choice_id = params[:chosen_section_id]
    unless sc.choice_ids.include?(choice_id)
      sc.choice_ids << choice_id
      sc.save!
    end
    respond_with({}, {location: ''})
  end
end
